vignette: A 60-year-old man has a complete ptosis of the right eye. When the lid is lifted the eye is turned down and out, and the pupil is 7 mm and unreactive. He has a severe headache.
stem: What is the most urgent diagnosis to exclude?
explanation: A painful third nerve palsy with a dilated fixed pupil means compression of the superficially placed pupillary fibers, classically by a posterior communicating aneurysm; a microvascular palsy usually spares the pupil. Emergency CTA is required.
